metadata.description: P4 — the prompty / prompter / pioneer / puppeteer meta-prompting framework; ships the Roboto four-lens reasoning instance and the standalone epistemic plugins (vlds, verification-discipline, emission-discipline, envelope-discipline) as installable plugins.

plugins.name: mister
plugins.description: Roboto / "The Init Elegance" — the four-lens reasoning instance of the P4 framework, built on the marketplace's standalone plugins: identity, rubric, orchestration, vlds, templates, bias-patterns, isomorphic-operations, sjc-indexer, activation, and persistence skills, plus a roboto subagent and the four P4 gate commands. It declares vlds, verification-discipline, emission-discipline, envelope-discipline, and src-fragger as dependencies, installed with it, and it is disabled while an installed copy sits below the version it is aligned to: its vlds skill binds the vlds plugin's gate, read barrier, guide, and inspector (CONFIRMED / PENDING / HEDGED), its templates release every fence under emission-discipline, and its activation gate never holds a verification. The subagent returns one report whose hand-back lists the pending acts, questions, and store proposals left for its caller; a session whose vlds index names it in `operator-via:` hands it every store moment, which it conducts through the vlds operator and its haiku puppets and returns as a derived understanding, never a response; its conductor skill fires only on the session's hand-off, never on the brief it gives the operator, and a return that is not the operator's derivation is relaunched once and reported. `p4.py` makes the closure model executable: it derives every closure from the skills' own `metadata.p4`, reconciles the rubric gate table against that graph so the puppeteer→prompty registration loop is machine-checked at both ends, and validates the plugin edge — every `<plugin>:<skill>` reference resolved through a declared dependency found in range, and each discipline's stage mapping checked against the phases of the skill that binds it.

plugins.name: vlds
plugins.description: VLDS — the P4 framework's epistemic discipline as a standalone, runtime dashboard of four instruments plus a conductor. The gate routes every load-bearing claim through VERIFIABLE → VERIFIED → CONFIRMED / PENDING / HEDGED — verify before you assert, state what you can't verify with its uncertainty attached. The guide loop disciplines the need behind the claim, configuring and recording the model's behavior as the user steers it. The inspector re-examines a high-stakes verdict through independent perspectives to corroborate, overturn, or surface it — the outside eye the others cannot be. The gc is a garbage collector for belief state, always on and modeled on V8's Oilpan (cppgc) — stored rules, memories, and training-data assumptions are marked LIVE / STALE / FREED-RESIDUE / UNOWNED by tracing reachability from a live root through handles (a paraphrase is a raw pointer the trace cannot see), swept transitively on a user retraction with every holder's pre-finalizer run in the turn of the free, compacted (the lesson survives, the directive dies), and tombstoned so the same garbage is not re-learned; its cycle rides the hooks every turn — roots marked at session start, the store traced concurrently by the operator, a write barrier tracing every store write, the precise collection at the turn's close — /vlds:gc full forces an atomic collection, /vlds:recall reads the cold archive on the owner's word alone, and /vlds:gc archive pours the whole hot tier into it, nothing exempt. The gate, guide and inspector are invoked directly, the gc runs always; a fifth skill, the looper, runs them in order, reading what the gc marked, and logs each decision to a shared, user-editable log. A SessionStart memory override extends the built-in per-project memory system like a derived class — base read/write untouched, the shared VLDS store living in the project's .claude/p4/sessions/<s8>/vlds/ directory, the gate's storage tiers persisted as per-tier partition files whose expiry the gc owns. The collector guards three barriers — read, write, and dispatch, the last catching a message addressed twice or one a later message already freed. No VLDS operation waits for the user's word or asks permission — each runs when owed, announced before and reported after; only version control and the disposal of what the user authored keep the per-act word. Five hooks carry the mechanical half — SessionStart injects the contract (in parts under the harness's hook-output cap), the gc's always-on block, a digest of the index, and an owner-voice digest, and hands every judged store operation to one operator subagent per session — launched at the first moment, continued for a bounded number of moments, then relaunched — whose derivation is what the session acts on: at the first prompt it takes the index's road — by default a script writes the pool's skeleton from the read barrier's own lines, one child reader per file on a cheap model picks what bears on the task, the script folds the picks in, and the operator streams its progress to the session as messages; or scripts/pick_model.py, a ranker trained on the store's own earlier pools, picking in the children's place (`pool-road: model`, measured against the children first under `model-shadow`; the dispatch barrier's own model, under `dispatch-model: on`, writing FRESH for a resembling message it is sure of, never a repeat, and the turn's close retraining either model in the background once the store outgrows it) — into one informed response scoped to the session's first task, which is what the session's context receives in place of the files; on a candidate row or an unknown short message it judges; when judged debt shows it scores what is cold and a script places it, while the close is a script applying the session's record, and the reply lists the derivation in one line at its top and, once its final plan is settled, that plan in one fence with no shell tag as short bullets before the first act, and a reply that ends with acts not done closes with the popup — one option per pending act, single-submit, re-served at every closing — whose selection is the word for exactly those acts; UserPromptSubmit stamps each message's dispatch row and runs the dispatch barrier's mechanical half (FRESH when no earlier row resembles the message, the candidate named otherwise, a known short command derived from the store's own adoption tokens), pours the dispatcher at a new session's first prompt, naming every session by its id and its chat title, and prints the last turn close's report; PreToolUse asks before a store-named file is written outside the store or a placeholder or guessed-ahead time is persisted, and denies — once per picker — an AskUserQuestion or show_widget call whose option briefs lack a standing label of briefs.md, where the close names what a picker left out when the owner had to ask (a detail-ask, stamped by the prompt hook; a label becomes standing at its second instance by the owner's ruling); PostToolUse runs the structural check, the whole verdict when it changed and one line when it did not, whose [STRAY] class names a store-shaped file found outside the store, then the gc's write barrier (phi.py trace: freed garbage allocated again, a new free's reach and its holders); Stop runs the trace once more and the light normalize sweep (attach, expire, the logger's overflow) through the register's gates — and every hook output carries the clock. The owner's standing rules reach every session whole in a SessionStart block of their own, whatever the pool's cap cuts. The pool's child readers run as the plugin's pick-reader agent, which has no tool that writes. An index's `operator-via:` names an agent the session hands every operator moment to instead, which launches the operator itself and returns a derived understanding while the response stays the session's. A conducted operator stays in its turn until every child has landed and returns only its derivation, never conducting another; without the Agent tool — none at spawn depth 3 — it picks for the files no child covered under pass heads, and the pool's read: line credits each file to its child, the pass, or none landed. The index's `index-engine:` moves the store, stage by stage, from the φ-register onto a keyspace indexed the way Chromium indexes IndexedDB — sorted plain-text keys, versions validated at read, journaled two-phase pours at any count, compaction when due, a verified gentle migration and a rollback — with the hot files, the barrier and the pool unchanged; by default a new store starts on the keyspace and a clean φ store migrates at its next turn close, and `index-engine: phi` keeps a store on the φ-register. Portable; no dependency on the roboto instance.

plugins.name: verification-discipline
plugins.description: Verification Discipline (truth-on-a-timer) — a standalone, self-obeying framework for WHEN a stale-or-wrong prior must be re-checked before it drives an action. Half-life decay classes decide when a prior has expired; an independent cost gate fires when a cheap canonical oracle exists for a load-bearing claim; confidence is barred as an input; and an action-scoped layer-priority rule keeps a stale policy from suppressing the check (verification is never insubordination). Sixteen rules in three groups, three mottos, and the live failure case they were derived from. Companion to the vlds gate — the when-to-verify policy behind it, not a second gate. Standalone; no external plugin dependencies.

plugins.name: emission-discipline
plugins.description: Emission Discipline (prose-may-hedge-fences-execute) — a standalone, self-obeying framework for WHAT the model is licensed to RELEASE into a code fence, and thus into user-owned systems. Models the experienced integration defect as (correct form available in-model) × (release layer that never checks the emission against it) — knowledge–emission divergence — and gates on what is about to be released, never on how casual the request was: eight defect classes by transmission vector, twenty-three rules in seven groups (mid-stream, turn-boundary, standing, mandate/license, session, delivery form — the final message after the turn's last tool call being the delivery surface, the final message opening with a Deviations block that names every self-decided departure or says none — ask), a resident trigger table, a PreToolUse fence gate that asks before a persisted fence carries a hedged literal, a deployment residency map, and the two live case studies it was derived from and amended against. Consequential-side twin of verification-discipline: that framework gates what the model believes, this one gates what it releases. Ships the doctrine as a direct-invoke skill plus a resident-gate wrapper skill for user-level installs. Standalone; no external plugin dependencies.

plugins.name: src-fragger
plugins.description: src-fragger (frags-outlive-the-session) — every piece of code the agent writes to complete a task, anything that replaces manual, user-involved labor with a script the agent builds and runs and whose job no single tool call does (an edit, an append, a whole-file write, or one shell command is the tool's own call, never a frag; a script that does the tool's job because a heredoc failed on the text is the call in costume), is a frag, and a frag is written to the VLDS p4/src/ directory and registered in src/frags.md, never to a scratchpad or a temp directory. The split is by worth, not by file type: the project's .claude/scratchpad/ is the always-notebook (tracked by the p4 repo) (notes, plans, commit messages, logs, captured output, downloads kept for reading — the SessionStart hook seeds a .gitignore of * inside it, so it ignores itself whatever the project's own rules say), and .claude/p4/src/ is the git-tracked home of every reusable and worthwhile output of that work, code or not: the frags in the task's directory, registered, and what they read or produced that is worth keeping — a fetched spec, a captured page, a downloaded source, a design spec, a run's report — in the task's out/ (src/<task>/out/), tracked and unregistered; a notebook file that turns out to be worth keeping — one a later task runs, reads or edits, or a commit is about to carry — graduates to src/ (code) or the task's out/ (anything else), a log a claim cites stays a note (the claim's entry carries what was read; the instrument that produced it is the output), nothing in the notebook is force-added to git, and a truly throwaway probe may stay there after the gate's ask. The harness scratchpad dies with the session and the notebook lives on one disk; a frag outlives both, so the next task updates it instead of rewriting it, the user can read and edit it (an edit is a ruling), and when the harness refuses the agent's own execution the frag is already where the user can run it — and before any hand-off the agent double-checks that the frag is registered, that the refusal survives a retry of the same call in a fresh tool call (a refusal is bound to the conversation's content — a fresh call or a fresh conversation can pass where a resume does not), that the user's word already covers the act, and that the interruption is a decision rather than labor. A SessionStart hook injects the contract, seeds the register and the notebook's .gitignore, says in one line when the project's root rules ignore src/ itself (never editing them), and in one more when src/ holds code the register does not name or the register names a path that is gone and not retired; a PreToolUse gate asks before a code file — by extension, a page included, or by a name such as CMakeLists.txt — is written to a temp location or to any project's .claude/scratchpad/. Shares the VLDS store; no other dependency.

plugins.name: envelope-discipline
plugins.description: Envelope Discipline (futures-land-as-fields) — a standalone, self-obeying framework for HOW a seam's configurables are shaped at the moment the seam is minted. Models interface calcification as (first-of-family mistaken for the whole story) × (no envelope reserved at the only cheap moment) and gates on what is about to be MINTED: the first option reveals the family and gets one named options envelope at birth; defaults are the null ask so no default carries doctrine; futures land as new named fields, never as signature breaks or per-knob rulings; the shape spans every layer of the seam, wire grammar included. Twelve rules in three groups, three mottos, and the live minting failure they were derived from. Shape-side sibling of verification-discipline (what may be believed) and emission-discipline (what may be released): this framework gates the contracts the other two operate across. Standalone; no external plugin dependencies.

plugins.name: p4-memory
plugins.description: p4-memory — the built-in per-project memory (the base class the vlds override wraps) is stored in the p4 repo, <project>/.claude/p4/memory/, never only in the device's local AppData: at every session start the AppData memory directory is copied in (a differing file kept in .conflicts/ for the owner's merge), renamed aside whole and replaced by a directory junction (a symlink off Windows) to the p4 copy, so the harness reads and writes p4 through its own fixed path; the rename is retried (the harness can hold the directory open at a session start), and until the link exists a PostToolUse mirror copies every memory written in AppData into p4 at once and the turn's close retries the link. Depends on vlds.

plugins.name: mind-reader
plugins.description: mind-reader — a side agent, detached from the session's conversation, that predicts what the OWNER will say next (never what the AI wants) and learns from how each prediction scored. The prompt hook scores the previous turn's frozen prediction against the owner's actual message, appends it to the session's vlds partition mind-reader.md (a gc-collectable object store of the keyspace), moves each source's learned weight (follow, progress, direction, adopt — a multiplicative-weights step) in .claude/p4/mrindex/model.json, then spawns a detached watcher and prints nothing, so the session answers uninterrupted. The watcher re-predicts while the turn runs into a rotating draft (sessions/<name>/mind-reader/draft.md) from every session's dispatch record and what the owner will be reacting to; the Stop hook freezes it, and writes gc holds (.claude/p4/vindex/holds.tsv) for the hot entries the owner's predicted direction leans on, which the vlds light pass and judged sweep skip until they expire — retention only, the archive ignoring them. A plain process: no model, no network, nothing written into the conversation.

plugins.name: flight-ops
plugins.description: flight-ops — flight operations for the p4 plugins' own operators, as they run: the VLDS operator, roboto as its conductor, the operator's pick-readers, the inspector's perspectives, and an orchestration branch run as an agent. Each is a flight with its own takeoff checklist (the brief its contract prescribes with the operator line's store, session, copied now and moment; the agent type and the recall config's model; foreground or background as the pool's road says; launch once, continue, then relaunch), its own landing (the return shape its brief promises: derivation, derived understanding, picks), its own go-around and lost-communications rule, a recorder line in the session's .claude/p4/sessions/<name>/flights.tsv, and an incident loop that hands every miss to the vlds ledger as a correction and amends the checklist with a test. A PreToolUse hook checks a recognized operator launch against its takeoff checklist and bounces a failing one once, the re-issue passing; a PostToolUse hook checks a foreground return's opening — an asynchronous one's on its agent-message hand-back, matched by agent id — and says a go-around in one line. Not a plan system: a launch that is not a p4 operator's passes untouched, and a failure inside the hook passes the call.
